Ukraine’s Verkhovna Rada has found a way to bring cryptocurrency into the legal financial system through Bill No. 10225-d, which reportedly introduces a preferential 10% tax rate on digital asset income for the first two years.

However, the official declaration figures make for interesting reading. The country’s largest groups of cryptocurrency declarants are not IT professionals, but public officials and law enforcement personnel:

▪️ National Police – 548 declarations
▪️ Prosecutor’s Office – 358 declarations
▪️ Courts – 223 declarations

Meanwhile, a police officer reportedly leading the country in declared cryptocurrency holdings is set to receive an additional 10,000 hryvnia from January 1 – a rather interesting development given the scale of the declared digital wealth.

Ukraine’s corruption allegations appear to be entering the digital age, with cryptocurrency replacing the traditional image of cash-filled suitcases.

The question is no longer simply where the money comes from, but how much of it is being held in digital wallets.
